title: Particle theory of matter
competency: State the postulates of the particle theory of matter.

keywords.def: A theory that explains matter as tiny moving particles with spaces and forces between them.
A main idea of a theory.

ideas.name: The six ideas of the particle model

en.text: The particle model has six main ideas. All matter is made of tiny particles. The particles move all the time. There are spaces between them. Heating makes them move faster. There are forces between them. Particles of one substance differ from those of another.

screens.title: Where did the sugar go?
screens.ask: Sugar dissolves in tea and seems to disappear. Where did it go?
opts: Its tiny particles spread into the spaces between water particles
screens.after: Sugar is still there: you can taste it. Its particles moved into spaces between the water particles.
screens.best: Its tiny particles spread into the spaces between water particles

screens.title: 2.1.3 Particle theory of matter
paras: Particulate nature of matter means all matter is made of tiny particles.
Many years later, scientists went back to Democritus' idea and added to it.
The theory they made is the particle model of matter.

screens.title: Main ideas (postulates) of the particle model
table: All matter is made up of tiny particles.
The particles of matter move continuously.
The particles have spaces between them.
Adding heat to matter makes the particles move faster.
There are forces between the particles.
Particles of one substance differ from the particles of other substances.
screens.note: Democritus was an ancient Greek thinker. He first said matter is made of tiny pieces.

screens.title: Six postulates, six examples
screens.ask: Tap each postulate to see it in daily life.
items: All matter is made of tiny particles. Even a stone or a drop of water.
The particles move continuously. A smell spreads across the room.
There are spaces between particles. Sugar fits into the spaces in tea.
Adding heat makes particles move faster. Ink spreads faster in hot water.
There are forces between particles. They hold a stone together.
Particles of salt differ from particles of water.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A theory that explains matter as tiny moving particles with spaces and forces between them.
A main idea of a theory.

screens.text: Particle model: which one is a postulate (main idea)?
screens.why:
Check each option against the six postulates.
"Particles never move" goes against postulate 2.
"All particles are the same" goes against postulate 6.
"Heat makes particles stop" goes against postulate 4.
Postulate 3 says there are spaces between particles. That is the answer.

screens.text: True or false (particle model): adding heat to matter makes its particles move faster.
screens.why:
Heat is a form of energy.
Particles that gain energy move faster.
This is postulate 4 of the particle model.
So the statement is true.
screens.clue: Think of hot and cold water.

screens.text: True or false (particle model): particles of water are the same as particles of salt.
screens.why:
Water and salt are different substances.
Postulate 6: particles of one substance differ from those of another.
So water particles are not salt particles.
The statement is false.
screens.clue: Is water the same substance as salt?

pairs: Sugar seems to disappear in tea
Steam escapes fast from hot water
A smell spreads in a room
screens.why:
Sugar "disappears" in tea: its particles fill spaces between water particles.
Steam escapes fast from hot water: heat makes particles move faster.
A smell spreads: particles move all the time.
A stone holds together: forces pull its particles together.
screens.text: Match each everyday event to the postulate that explains it.
Spaces between particles: a syringe full of air can be pushed in, but a syringe full of sand hardly moves. Which postulate explains the air?
opts: There are big spaces between gas particles
screens.ans: There are big spaces between gas particles
screens.why:
Air is a gas: its particles are far apart.
Pushing the plunger moves them into the empty spaces.
Sand grains already touch, so there is little space to close.
So the answer is: there are big spaces between gas particles.
screens.clue: What is between the air particles?

items.title: 1. List the postulates of particle theory (book order)
items: All matter is made up of tiny particles.
The particles of matter move continuously.
The particles have spaces between them.
Adding heat makes the particles move faster.
There are forces between the particles.
Particles of one substance differ from others.
items.why:
1: start with what matter is: tiny particles.
2: how they behave: they move all the time.
3: what is between them: spaces.
4: what heat does: makes them move faster.
5: what holds them: forces.
6: how substances differ: different particles.
items.clue: Start with what matter is made of.

items.text: Exercise 2.2: describe the particulate nature of matter.
opts: All matter is made of discrete tiny particles
items.ans: All matter is made of discrete tiny particles
items.why:
Particulate means "made of particles".
All matter, solid, liquid or gas, is made of tiny separate (discrete) particles.
"Only gases have particles" is wrong: solids and liquids have them too.
Answer: all matter is made of discrete tiny particles.

test.text: True or false: according to the particle model, particles of matter move continuously.
test.why:
Postulate 2: the particles of matter move continuously.
Dust in the wind and spreading smells show this.
So the statement is true.

test.text: How many main ideas (postulates) does the book list for the particle model?
test.why:
Count the book's list.
1 tiny particles, 2 always moving, 3 spaces between them.
4 heat makes them faster, 5 forces between them, 6 substances differ.
So there are 6 postulates.

test.text: Particle model: which postulate explains why particles of salt differ from particles of sugar?
opts: Particles of one substance differ from those of another
test.ans: Particles of one substance differ from those of another
test.why:
Salt and sugar are two different substances.
Postulate 6: particles of one substance differ from those of other substances.
That is why salt particles differ from sugar particles.

test.ask: Particle model: there are ___ between the particles that hold them together.
test.why:
Something holds a stone's particles together.
Postulate 5: there are forces between the particles.
Answer: forces.

test.text: Particle model: ink spreads faster in hot water than in cold water. Which postulate explains this?
test.why:
Step 1: hot water particles have more energy.
Step 2: more energy means faster particles (postulate 4).
Step 3: faster particles mix the ink more quickly.
Answer: heat makes particles move faster.

notes.text: The book says "scientists came back to Democritus' idea" without introducing Democritus. A one-line note is added (ancient Greek thinker). Teacher to confirm.
